creator: Alexander Terp
description:
On a Linux pane, `muster pane send --confirm` and the API's confirmed `pane.send` answer done for a line over 4095 bytes sent to a program reading in canonical mode, though the program received the line cut short. Measured 2026-11-01 in the Debian container `./dev --linux` uses: a line of 4200 x's and `end`, sent to `cat`, reached it as its first 4095 bytes and a newline, while the terminal echoed the whole line, `end` included. The read-back finds the line's tail in that echo, so it confirms a line that did not arrive whole. Lines of up to 4095 bytes arrive whole, and so do the lines sent after a long one.

macOS behaves as `docs/cli/limits.md` says: it echoes the first 1024 bytes, delivers none of the line, and drops what is sent after it. That page and the refusal reason in `crates/muster-core/src/pane_text.rs` give macOS's 1024 bytes as every terminal's limit, so both are wrong for a Linux devenv pane.

Found while fixing a_2sC9MUeZK, whose test sent `cat` a 1103-byte line and expected the macOS refusal.
title: --confirm reports a long line done on a Linux pane that received only its first 4095 bytes
